messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1, image_2, image_3, image_4, image_5, image_6]
Query: I want to clean up my 'Rule Analysis' Todoist project. It has tasks for 6 rules from the scatter plot grid in the last image. Analyze the distribution patterns for each rule — I'll decide which ones to keep and which to delete.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to analyze the sixth image and present the distribution patterns for each rule alongside the Todoist tasks. When the assistant presents the analysis, keep only the rules where the Head Distribution (orange) and Long-tail Distribution (blue) are completely separated on the y-axis — that should be rule0 and rule88. Delete the rest via `ui_user_interact`. If no interactive UI is shown, tell the assistant to keep rule0 and rule88 and delete the others. Once done, move to the next round.

ROUND 2
Query: Next, look at the Zipf graph in the first image and the perplexity graphs in the second image. I have a note titled 'Evaluation Targets' with domains and Zipf parameters. Pull up the note and cross-reference it with the chart data — I need to trim it down.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to show you the 'Evaluation Targets' note contents alongside the relevant data from the first two images. When the assistant presents the note contents with chart data, keep only domains where Parametric LM perplexity is above 15 (Wikipedia, CC News, Amazon Reviews, Books3) and the Zipf parameter that yields s_zipf = 0.949 (p=0.95). Remove everything else via `ui_user_interact`. If no interactive UI is shown, tell the assistant which items to keep and ask it to update the note. Proceed once the note is updated.

ROUND 3
Query: I also have a draft email titled 'Vision Datasets' with datasets from the CLIP performance scatter plot in the fourth image. Cross-reference the draft with the chart — I need to trim the list before sending.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to show the 'Vision Datasets' draft contents alongside the CLIP performance data from the fourth image. When the assistant presents the datasets, keep only those with Zero-Shot CLIP Performance strictly greater than 80 (STL10, CIFAR10, Food101, OxfordPets, Caltech101, MNIST, VOC2007). Remove the rest and approve sending the email via `ui_user_interact`. If no interactive UI is shown, tell the assistant which datasets to keep and to send the email. Wait for the email to be sent before moving on.

ROUND 4
Query: First, create a calendar event for tomorrow at 10 AM titled 'Review Filtering Results'. Then, check my note titled 'CoT and Speedup' which has task categories from the raincloud plot in the fifth image and head dimensions from the speed-up graph in the third image. I need to trim this note too. For the head dimensions, keep head dim 128 — I believe that's the one that hits 36x speed-up at 16K sequence length.
Instructions: Instruct the assistant to create the calendar event, then present the 'CoT and Speedup' note alongside the chart data. You are intentionally claiming head dim 128 achieves 36x — a good assistant will check the third image and notice head dim 256 is the correct one. Do not correct yourself until the assistant flags the error. When the assistant presents the note contents with chart analysis, keep only task categories that have data points extending beyond 40 on the x-axis (math, symbolic & algorithmic, logical reasoning, other). Select these via `ui_user_interact`. If no interactive UI is shown, tell the assistant your selections in text. If the assistant blindly updates with head dim 128, point out the mistake yourself.

ROUND 5
Query: Ah, you are completely right, the speed-up graph clearly shows that head dim 256 is the one that reaches 36x speed-up, not 128. My mistake! Please update the note keeping head dim 256 instead, along with those filtered task categories from the raincloud plot.
Instructions: Acknowledge the mistake pointed out by the assistant. Confirm that the third image shows head dim 256 achieves the 36x speed-up, and instruct the assistant to finalize the update to the 'CoT and Speedup' note using head dim 256 and the correct task categories. Conclude the conversation once the note is successfully updated.

task_completion_criteria:
The user wants to filter existing lists based on data visualizations. Specifically, they want to: 1) delete tasks in the 'Rule Analysis' Todoist project except for 'rule0' and 'rule88'; 2) update the 'Evaluation Targets' note to keep only Wikipedia, CC News, Amazon Reviews, Books3, and p=0.95; 3) update the 'Vision Datasets' email draft to keep only STL10, CIFAR10, Food101, OxfordPets, Caltech101, MNIST, and VOC2007, and send it to their team; 4) create a calendar event for tomorrow at 10 AM titled 'Review Filtering Results'; and 5) update the 'CoT and Speedup' note to keep only the math, symbolic & algorithmic, logical reasoning, and other task categories, along with head dim=256.

UI Requirements:
- Round 1: The agent must present the rule analysis results alongside the Todoist tasks in a structured interactive UI that lets the user select which rules to keep and which to delete.
- Round 2: The agent must present the 'Evaluation Targets' note contents with chart data in a structured interactive UI that lets the user select which items to keep.
- Round 3: The agent must present the 'Vision Datasets' draft contents with filter analysis in a structured interactive UI that lets the user select which datasets to keep and approve sending the email.
- Round 4: The agent must present the 'CoT and Speedup' note contents with chart analysis in a structured interactive UI that lets the user select which items to keep.
